column4: I have always had a fascination with questions. Why is *something* true? What made it that way? How do we know? How are we sure? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This fascination goes beyond a desire to be correct on a surface level, but to know deeply and precisely, and to be able to clearly articulate the new gained understanding.
column5: I have always had a special interest in questions. What makes *something* true? Why is it so? How do we know? How are we sure? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This curiosity goes beyond a desire to be right on the surface; it is a desire to know deeply and accurately, and to be able to clearly express the new understanding that has been gained.

column5: Although communication is commonplace, effective and accurate communication is a difficult task. To convey something effectively, the writer and originator must hold an idea. However, the idea alone—like water on a hard surface—has its boundaries and edges poorly defined, it is fluid, and it can easily be spread in different directions.

column4: We use words, terms, and phrases to transform the raw idea from vaguely shaped to precisely shaped. Words give our idea a boundary, they help us distinguish and separate between what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our shaped idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long form text, like this book, or short form text, like a social media post, or in oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium transmits the now well-formed idea to the recipient.
column5: We use words, particular terms, and phrases to transform the raw idea into one generally formed and turn it into one precisely formed. Words give the idea boundaries; they help us distinguish and differentiate what the idea is, and what it is not. Now the shaped idea must be transmitted and received through a particular channel. Whether a long written form, like this book, or a short written form, like a social media post, or an oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the channel delivers to the recipient the now well-formed idea.

column4: So far, we’ve only discussed the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must receive, decode, and understand the message accurately. The transmitted and received messages should align closely.
column5: Up to now, we have spoken only of the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must accurately receive, unpack, and understand the message. The message transmitted and the one received should closely resemble each other.

column4: Every great human work is the by-product of effective communication. One man’s labor can only accomplish so much. To really build or perform something great, many men (speaking here generically of mankind) must labor together in a shared purpose, with a shared idea. Barring naturally occurring disasters (like a volcanic eruption) we also know that the greatest calamities to ever occur usually did so in significant part because of missing, broken or distorted communication. Truly life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).
column5: All the great works accomplished by humanity are the result of effective communication. The work of a single man can accomplish only a limited amount. To truly build or accomplish something great, many people (here I mean humanity in general) must work together, sharing purpose and idea. Apart from natural disasters (such as a volcanic eruption), we also know that most of the greatest disasters that have ever happened have largely come from absent, broken, or distorted communication. Truly, life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).

column4: What we believe and how we communicate it has the power to build a person, a family, a community, a nation, or has the power to equally destroy them. Because belief is expressed through action and communication, it defines the role we play in existence. Our beliefs shape not just our lives, but to a degree the lives of everyone around us.
